subject: DI04005021

body.en:
Definition / principle

Phase equilibrium is a state with no net transfer tendency for a species between contacting phases at the specified state; its chemical potentials are equal across the interface.

Detailed theory and conditions

Equilibrium does not require equal concentrations in gas and liquid. A relation such as y*=mx connects the gas composition in equilibrium with a liquid composition; the asterisk means the corresponding equilibrium value, not a measured bulk value. For absorption, ybulk exceeding y*(xbulk) gives a gas-to-liquid tendency. A plot must identify temperature, pressure, composition basis and species; changing these changes the equilibrium relation. Local interface equilibrium is a two-film model assumption and need not mean the entire equipment is at equilibrium. If the bulk phases already match their equilibrium relation, the driving force vanishes even though molecules still move in both directions.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Specified state પર contacting phases વચ્ચે species ની net transfer tendency ન હોય તે phase equilibrium છે. Interface ની બંને બાજુ chemical potentials સમાન હોય છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Equilibrium માં gas/liquid concentrations સમાન હોવી જરૂરી નથી. y*=mx જેવી relation liquid composition સાથે equilibrium gas composition જોડે છે. Asterisk corresponding equilibrium value છે, measured bulk value નહીં. Absorption માટે ybulk>y*(xbulk) હોય તો gas-to-liquid tendency છે. Plot પર T, P, species તથા composition basis લખો; તે બદલાય તો equilibrium relation બદલાય છે. Two-film model માં local interface equilibrium assumption છે; સમગ્ર equipment equilibrium માં નથી. Bulk phases equilibrium relation satisfy કરે ત્યારે net driving force zero થાય છે છતાં molecular motion ચાલુ રહે છે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

title.en: Two-film concept and local versus overall coefficients

h.en: Two-film concept and local versus overall coefficients

body.en:
Definition / principle

The two-film model represents resistance on both sides of an interface by gas-side and liquid-side films. A local coefficient uses bulk-to-interface driving force; an overall coefficient uses an equivalent bulk-to-bulk driving force.

Detailed theory and conditions

A gas solute diffuses through the gas film, passes an interface assumed at equilibrium and diffuses into the liquid bulk. At steady interfacial transfer without accumulation, the flux through both films is equal, not the compositions. In the mole-fraction convention, ky and kx have units molar flux per mole fraction. KG based on pressure and kL based on liquid molar concentration have different dimensions; never add their reciprocal resistances without the appropriate equilibrium conversion. Overall coefficients avoid the usually unmeasured interface compositions but still depend on both film resistances and the equilibrium slope. For nonlinear equilibrium use a suitable local slope/segment and do not insert one arbitrary constant m across the whole column.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Two-film model માં interface ની બંને બાજુ gas તથા liquid films થી resistances દર્શાવાય છે. Local coefficient bulk-to-interface driving force અને overall coefficient equivalent bulk-to-bulk driving force વાપરે છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Gas solute gas film માંથી interface સુધી અને પછી liquid film માંથી bulk માં જાય છે. Interface equilibrium માનવામાં આવે છે. Steady condition માં બંને film ના flux સમાન છે, compositions નહીં. Mole-fraction convention માં ky, kx ના units flux per mole fraction છે. Pressure-based KG તથા concentration-based kL ના dimensions જુદા છે; equilibrium conversion વગર reciprocals ન ઉમેરો. Overall coefficients અજાણ interface compositions ટાળે છે, પરંતુ બંને resistances તથા equilibrium slope પર આધારિત છે. Nonlinear relation માટે યોગ્ય local slope/segment લો; સમગ્ર column માટે arbitrary m ન મૂકો.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady transfer A from gas to liquid; no interfacial accumulation/reaction; linear local equilibrium yi=mxi with constant positive m; same molar-flux and mole-fraction bases throughout.

  1. Write gas-side and liquid-side drops.

  2. Split the gas-based overall driving force.

  3. Use interface and conjugate bulk equilibrium.

  4. Substitute film drops.

  5. Compare with the overall gas-side definition.

  6. For the liquid basis, split x*−x and divide the gas drop by m.

  7. The liquid overall result and conversion follow.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: write film fluxes → split gas driving force → convert liquid drop by m → reciprocal resistance result. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.
body.gu:
સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Gas માંથી liquid માં A નો steady transfer; interface accumulation/reaction નહીં. yi=mxi તથા positive constant m લો. બધાં coefficients માટે same molar-flux/mole-fraction basis રાખો.

  1. Gas તથા liquid film ના drops લખો.

  2. Gas-based overall driving force split કરો.

  3. Interface તથા conjugate bulk equilibrium લો.

  4. Film drops મૂકો.

  5. Overall gas-side definition સાથે સરખાવો.

  6. Liquid basis માટે x*−x split કરીને gas drop ને m થી ભાગો.

  7. Liquid overall result તથા conversion મળે છે.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

title.gu: Coefficients ના Uses તથા Controlling Resistance

h.gu: Coefficients ના Uses તથા Controlling Resistance

body.en:
Definition / principle

The controlling resistance is the film contribution dominating the overall resistance on a consistently chosen driving-force basis.

Detailed theory and conditions

On the gas basis compare1/ky with m/kx, not ky and kx alone. If the gas contribution dominates, increasing gas-side mixing/area is more helpful than improving an already negligible liquid resistance. If the liquid contribution dominates, liquid mixing and interfacial renewal may help. A small equilibrium slope generally favors gas-side control; large m may emphasize liquid-side resistance, but actual coefficients must still be compared. Local coefficients are useful for correlations and identifying film effects; overall coefficients are convenient in design/rate measurements using accessible bulk samples. Neither a larger coefficient nor equilibrium data alone specifies the total transfer without area and a compatible driving force.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Consistent driving-force basis પર overall resistance માં જે film contribution સૌથી મોટું હોય તે controlling resistance છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Gas basis પર 1/ky તથા m/kx સરખાવો; ફક્ત ky, kx નહીં. Gas resistance dominant હોય તો gas-side mixing/area સુધારવું વધુ ઉપયોગી છે. Liquid resistance dominant હોય તો liquid mixing/interface renewal મદદ કરે છે. Small equilibrium slope gas-side control ને favor કરી શકે; large m liquid resistance વધારી શકે, પરંતુ actual terms સરખાવવા પડે. Local coefficients correlations/film effects માટે અને overall coefficients accessible bulk samples થી rate/design માટે ઉપયોગી છે. Coefficient અથવા equilibrium data એકલાં total transfer આપતાં નથી; area તથા compatible driving force જોઈએ.

title.en: Ideal stage,stage efficiency and cascade types
title.gu: Ideal Stage,Stage Efficiency તથા Cascade Types

h.en: Ideal stage,stage efficiency and cascade types
h.gu: Ideal Stage,Stage Efficiency તથા Cascade Types

body.en:
Definition / principle

An ideal equilibrium stage brings the departing phases to equilibrium. An actual stage provides finite contact and may approach that limit only partly. A cascade is an interconnected series of contacting stages.

Detailed theory and conditions

Overall tray efficiency is the number of theoretical stages divided by the actual stages for the same duty. Murphree gas efficiency compares the actual gas-composition change with the ideal change relative to liquid leaving that tray; it is not the same as total solute recovery. Countercurrent cascades send phases oppositely and commonly maintain useful driving forces with lower solvent demand. Co-current cascades send both phases in the same direction and approach a common equilibrium limit. Crosscurrent extraction contacts successive raffinate streams with fresh solvent portions; the solvent extracts leave separately unless combined downstream. Always state which efficiency and composition basis are being used.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Departing phases ને equilibrium સુધી લાવતો stage ideal equilibrium stage છે. Actual stage finite contact થી તે limit સુધી આંશિક પહોંચે છે. Interconnected contacting stages ની series cascade છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Same duty માટે theoretical stages ને actual stages થી ભાગો તે overall tray efficiency છે. Murphree gas efficiency actual gas-composition change ને tray છોડી રહેલા liquid સાથે equilibrium ideal change સામે સરખાવે છે; તે total solute recovery નથી. Countercurrent માં phases opposite જાય છે તથા solvent demand ઘણી વખત ઓછી રહે છે. Co-current માં same direction માં જઈ common equilibrium limit તરફ પહોંચે છે. Crosscurrent extraction માં successive raffinate ને fresh solvent portions મળે છે અને extracts અલગ નીકળે છે. કઈ efficiency તથા composition basis છે તે સ્પષ્ટ કરો.
